MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 11, 2020

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:01 p.m., on February 11, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 6, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  Council Member Sachs

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Liability Claims: Claimants: Donaldson, Orloff, Gray and Peterson: Agency Claimed
  Against-City of Mission Viejo and: Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to
  Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9. (4 cases)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Sachs was
absent).

City Council Minutes  1  February 11, 2020
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received updates and provided direction to
staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Goodell presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Mark Anthony Duran, and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Corporal
  Kurt A. Koehler.

P2. New Voting Options for 2020

  Registrar of Voters Operations Manager Justin Berardino made the presentation and
  answered questions from the City Council.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Shelby Garrison M.V.: Asked that the Council consider paving the La Paws Dog Park parking
lot.

Paul Watrous, M.V.: Announced that he has received violation letters from Code Enforcement
stating that his personal vehicle, a 2014 Ford F150 Truck, is not compliant with the City’s
Municipal Code regarding parking of commercial vehicles. He said he disagrees and asked that
the matter be resolved.

Danny Gray, Capo Beach: Spoke in favor of Community Choice Energy (CCE) which allows
residents to choose their own source of energy. He encouraged the City to look into opportunities
with CCE.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Sachs

1.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  2  February 11, 2020
   Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 28, 202, as
  presented

2.  Check Register Dated January 17, 2020 in the Amount of $3,195,499.11

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated January 24, 2020 in the Amount of $516,406.48

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2019

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for December 2019

  Received and filed.

6.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for December 2019

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December
  2019

  Received and filed.

8.  Lease of Replacement Storage Systems

  (1) Approved entrance into 5-year lease agreement with Arrow Capital Solutions and CDW
  for purchase of Pure Storage, Inc. storage system and issuance of purchase orders to Arrow
  Capital Solutions, Inc. annually in the amount of $71,290.58 for a total lease of $356,452.90,
  and (2) approved a 2% purchase contingency and allow staff to complete and approve any
  additional lease documents not included with this report but which fall within the cost
  parameters provided.

9.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending December 31, 2019

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending
  December 31, 2019.

10. Felipe Road & Olympiad Road Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 19837) - Notice of
  Completion

City Council Minutes  3  February 11, 2020
   (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

11. Via Fabricante Area Catch Basin Debris Screens (CIP 20241) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

12. Craycraft Park Restroom Construction – (CIP 315)

  Awarded contract to A 2 Z Construct, Inc. for the construction of Craycraft Park Restroom
  in an amount not to exceed $166,675.00.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

13. Angled Parking on Via Fabricante – Post-Implementation Evaluation

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  preserve the angled parking on Via Fabricante and implement traffic calming in the form of
  electronic speed feedback signs and reduction of the posted speed limit from 35 mph to 30
  mph; and (2) introduce Ordinance 20-336 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission
  Viejo Municipal Code Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

City Council Minutes  4  February 11, 2020
 STAFF REPORTS

15. FY 2019-2020 Golf Course Operations Budget

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson gave the staff report.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay displayed a PowerPoint
  presentation on the golf course sustainability.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to ratify
  the FY 2019-2020 Golf Course Operations Budget for November 9, 2019 through June 30,
  2020.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record

Council Member Bucknum

17. Environmental Concerns (Open House Gas) and the Preservation of Environmentally
  Sensitive Alternative Energy Sources

  Council Member Bucknum and City Attorney Bill Curley presented the report.

  Michael Rotcher, M.V.: Stated that he feels this resolution is a ploy by the Gas Industry to
  promote their natural gas interests. He said he is in favor of Community Choice Energy
  (CCE).

  Jose Trinidad Castaneda, Fullerton: Congratulated the Council for discussing energy choices
  and spoke in favor of CCE.

  Ayn Cracium, Irvine: Spoke on safety issues with natural gas and voiced her support for
  CCE.

  Margo Finlayson, Lake Forest: Stated that the resolution does not represent true choice and
  she feels that it was prompted by Southern California Gas Company. Ms. Finlayson spoke
  about fossil fuels, renewable energy jobs and expressed support for CCE.

City Council Minutes  5  February 11, 2020
   Kari Dietrich, Irvine: Spoke about climate change across the globe and said that fossil fuels
  are the key detrimental contributors to climate change. She also expressed her preference for
  CCE.

  Paul Berry, Santa Ana: Spoke in favor of CCE and asked that the Council vote no on this
  resolution.

  Justin Bass, M.V. Referred to various articles on solar electricity and expressed concerns
  with fossil fuel-caused climate crisis’. He said that moving towards electric vehicles and solar
  electricity will be beneficial for future generations because it is cleaner and cheaper.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Goodell, Adopt
  Resolution 20-04 Supporting Maintaining Local Control of Energy Solutions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell and Kelley
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  Sachs

Council Member Bucknum discussed her attendance at an event honoring Orange County Fire
Authority employees, two of whom were from Mission Viejo. She pointed out that there are a
significant number of firefighters residing within Mission Viejo. Council Member Bucknum
reminded residents that Valentine’s Day is Friday and she encouraged residents to spend their
money within the City. She noted a few hidden gem restaurants: O’Neill’s Grill at the Arroyo
Trabuco Country Club, Dublin 4 and Wineworks on Oso Parkway, and High Park Tap House, to
name a few. Council Member Bucknum concluded by wishing everyone a happy Valentine’s Day
and Health Heart Awareness Month.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths invited residents to attend the Mission Viejo Rotary Club Breakfast at the
Mission Viejo Country Club, every Wednesday morning at 7:00 a.m. He noted that there are about
45 members in this service organization that helps the community and local schools.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley shared the 2019 Annual Report and gave special thanks to Director of
Community Relations Karen Hamman for her great work with the publication. She said that this
report contains valuable information for residents and she encouraged them to obtain a copy.
Council Member Kelley reminded residents of the importance of voting and that there are changes
this year so make sure to read the election materials to learn when and where to vote. She
announced that she attended the Orange County Business Journal Presentation of the 13 CFOs of
the Year. She was there to support Amy Potter, CFO of The Toll Roads, who was one of seventy
CFOs that were nominated. She said that unbeknownst to her, one of the winning CFOs was one
of Mission Viejo’s Investment Advisory Commissioners, Elizabeth Pagliarini, who received a
Lifetime Achievement Award. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley concluded by congratulating Elizabeth on
her prestigious award.

City Council Minutes  6  February 11, 2020
 Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell announced last week he attended the South Orange County Mayors Association
meeting in Laguna Beach, along with City Manager Wilberg. He said that it was nice to get
together with other mayors and city managers in the region. He also attended the South Orange
County Watershed Executive Committee which focuses on the waterways leading down to the
Dana Point Harbor. He expressed the importance for Council Member participation with these
other jurisdictions so that the intent of the Clean Water Act is being met. Mayor Goodell stated
that he also attended the Orange County Fire Authority’s Best and Bravest Awards with Council
Member Bucknum where great service and public safety professionals were honored. He
announced that on Valentine’s Day, the Marguerite Aquatics Center will be holding the National
Age Group Championship which is a four-day swim meet. Lastly, he announced that the
Marguerite Aquatics Center will be holding the TYR Pro Swim Series April 16 through 19, 2020
and he encouraged residents to come out to see Olympic athletes compete.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:14 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 25, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 25, 2020

City Council Minutes  7  February 11, 2020
